title: Your Shares Just Got Faster: SEBI's Push for Instant Settlements

faq.q: What is 'settlement' in the stock market?
faq.a: Settlement is the process where the actual transfer of shares to the buyer's demat account and money to the seller's bank account is completed after a trade is executed.
Madhabi Puri Buch is the current Chairperson of the Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI), the primary regulator for the securities market in India.

faq.q: When will instantaneous settlement be fully implemented?
faq.a: SEBI is moving in phases. One-hour settlement is targeted by March (next year), which is a stepping stone towards full instantaneous settlement. The timeline for full instantaneous settlement is still being worked out with the ecosystem.

faq.q: How does this affect my existing investments?
faq.a: This change primarily affects how quickly new trades are settled. Your existing investments held in your demat account are not directly impacted by the settlement cycle change, but if you decide to sell them, you will have the option for faster settlement if they are among the eligible top 500 stocks.
